test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A and B alone can do a piece of work in 30 days and 40 days respectively. If they work on alternate days and B starts the work on the first day, then in how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
**Given:**

A alone can do the work in 30 days.

B alone can do the work in 40 days.

They work on alternate days, and B starts the work on the first day.

**Formula Used:**

Work done per day = Work done by A in 1 day + Work done by B in 1 day

Total Work = 1 (Complete Work)

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/30

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/40

Work done in 2 days (1 day by B and 1 day by A) = 1/40 + 1/30

Work done in 2 days = (1)/(40) + (1)/(30)

Work done in 2 days = (3 + 4)/(120)

Work done in 2 days = (7)/(120)

Let the number of complete 2-day cycles required be n.

Then, work done in n cycles = (7n)/(120)

To complete the work:

(7n)/(120) = 1

⇒ 7n = 120

⇒ n = (120)/(7)

⇒ n ≈ 17 (1/7)

So, the work completed in 17 cycles = 17 × 7 = 119

and remaining work = 120 - 119 = 1

Total days = 17 × 2 + time taken to complete the remaining 1 work.

Since the work is completed on the 1st day of the 18th cycle, the actual number of days taken is 34 + (1/3) day by B on the 35th day.

So, the work is completed in 34 (1)/(3) \ days.

**The correct answer is **34 (1)/(3) \ ** days.**
